subject: general
question: MS DOS is an operating system that has a/an:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Command Line Interface**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MS-DOS** is an operating system that has a **Command Line Interface**.
 
• It is a **Microsoft-developed operating system** for** x86-based personal computers**.
 
• It's rebranded as IBM PC DOS and a few operating systems that attempt to be compatible with MS-DOS are referred to as "DOS" together (which is also the generic acronym for disc operating system).
 
• During the 1980s, MS-DOS was the primary operating system for IBM PC compatibles, until it was gradually replaced by operating systems with a graphical user interface (GUI), such as the graphical Microsoft Windows operating system.
 
• A user is connected to a computer application or operating system via a command-line interface. Users interact with a system or programme by typing text into the CLI (commands). Following a visual prompt from the computer, the command is written on a specific line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A voice user interface (VUI) **allows people to communicate with computers by employing speech recognition to interpret instructions and respond to questions, as well as text-to-speech to playback responses.
 
• **A graphical user interface (GUI) **is a computer application that lets you connect with a computer using symbols, visual metaphors, and pointing devices.
 
• The Debian Free Software Guidelines were the inspiration for **the Open Source Definition**.
